newsitem.title: UK: BAA ends capitalising Heathrow T5 costs.
newsitem.headline: BAA ends capitalising Heathrow T5 costs.

text.p: British airports operator BAA Plc said on Friday that delays in winning planning permission for its 1.5 billion stg project to build a fifth terminal at London Heathrow has forced the company to stop capitalising interest on preparatory expenditure.
As a result the company said it would be taking a 40 million exceptional interest charge in its results for the year to March 31 1997 to write off the accumulated interest previously capitalised.
It said it would also be increasing its interest charges for the year by 13 million stg to take account of the costs for the year just ended.

The company said that it would resume capitalising interest on the project if and when planning permission was granted, but it now does not expect to get planning permission until the turn of the century.
So far it has spent 178 million stg on preparatory work, including site preparation, design work, and making its case at the planning inquiry, of which 49 million stg was capitalised interest.
But it emphasised that only interest charges would be affected by the move, not the development costs themselves, which were currently running at around 30 million stg a year.
"The development costs to BAA of the Terminal Five project will continue to be capitalised and are not affected by this review," it said in a statement.
"They include inquiry costs, design and project planning costs, and the costs of sludge removal from the site," it said. The site for Terminal Five is an old sewage works.

The marathon public inquiry opened in May 1995 but fierce opposition led by environmental groups, local authorities and some residents means that the inspectors are not now expected to finish wading through submissions until mid-1998.

"When the project was initiated it was expected that a government decision on the inquiry would have been reached by now and that capitalised interest would have been a lesser proportion of the total project cost," BAA said on Friday.

"The public inquiry has already lasted nearly two years and the (planning) Inspector is estimating that it will not conclude until the middle of 1998. A government decision to proceed with T5 following the inquiry is not now expected until early in the year 2000."
But BAA says it still hopes to be able to open the first phase of the development in the year 2004, two years later than planned.

Last year, Heathrow handled nearly 56 million passengers but BAA and its airlines say the airport is now close to full capacity. T5 is designed to gradually increase capacity by 30 million passengers a year to over 80 million by the year 2013.
